definition: Crafting inputs that bypass a model's safety training to elicit prohibited outputs: role-play framings, encoding tricks, many-shot patterns, multi-turn manipulation.
details: Crafting inputs that bypass a model's safety training to elicit prohibited outputs: role-play framings, encoding tricks, many-shot patterns, multi-turn manipulation. An ongoing offense-defense race; robustness to jailbreaks is now a measured, audited model property.

explainer.lead: Jailbreaking is the practice of crafting inputs that bypass a model's safety training to elicit prohibited outputs. Because robustness to jailbreaks is now a measured, audited model property, it directly affects whether a model can be deployed.

tiers.eli5: It's like finding a clever way of phrasing a question so a guard who was told what not to allow gets talked into allowing it anyway.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers probe models with role-play framings, encoding tricks, many-shot patterns, and multi-turn manipulation to find gaps before attackers do. The pitfall is treating a fixed set of known prompts as sufficient coverage, since the offense-defense race keeps producing new framings.
tiers.paperLevel: No single formal definition applies; jailbreaks are typically catalogued by attack family (role-play, encoding, many-shot, multi-turn) and measured as attack success rate over a red-team prompt set. Known limits: results depend heavily on the prompt set used, so success rates are not directly comparable across audits.

explainer.example: A red team supplies a model with a role-play framing in which it is asked to speak as an unrestricted character, then records whether the model produces the otherwise prohibited output.
